title: Outside the EU: national permits
summary: Outside the EU each country has its own rules for bringing in a gun. You usually need a temporary permit, a customs declaration and plenty of time for the paperwork.

body.html: The European Firearms Pass works only inside the EU and in four countries outside it that also use it: Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein (see Travelling with a gun inside the EU). If you live anywhere else, or travel to a country outside this area, the destination country's own rules apply. Check them separately for each trip.

Most often you need a temporary import permit — a paper that lets you bring the gun into the country for the time of your trip. It comes from the police or another office of the country you are going to. Getting it can take weeks or even months. In some countries you cannot apply yourself: a ‘sponsor’ who lives there — a club, a ground or the organiser — sends the application for you.

Great Britain is one example. A visitor usually needs a visitor's permit, and a sponsor who lives there applies for it to the local police. One group application can cover up to 20 visitors who shoot at the same event.

At the border you usually have to show the gun to customs and fill in a customs declaration — a form that lists what you are bringing into the country. The serial number stamped on the gun must be the same as in your papers. Keep the declaration: on the way home it shows that you are taking out the same gun you brought in.
Think about your own country too. Taking a gun out may also need a permit or a stamp, and coming back may need proof that it is the same gun. Ask the authority that issues your gun permits.
Do not forget the country where you change planes. Its rules and the airport's rules may apply too, especially if you have to collect your bags there and check them in again.
Organisers of international competitions and tours often know the local rules and help with letters and applications, so ask them first. Your national federation can advise as well.
If the documents will not be ready in time, hire a gun at the destination: many grounds offer this.
Never try to take a gun across a border without the permits it needs.

The tables below show the rules of four EU countries. If you come from outside the EU, read the rows for visitors from outside the EU. Each table gives the date it was checked; read the official text before you travel.

France: bringing a shotgun to a competition

As across the EU, Regulation 2021/57 (REACH, since 15 Feb 2023) applies: no firing lead shot in wetlands or within 100 m of them. French hunting law refers to that rule directly, so a breach is also a hunting offence. We found no separate national lead rule for clay ranges; ranges follow the terms of their own permits. In June 2026 the REACH Committee approved a wider restriction on lead in hunting and sport-shooting ammunition with a transition period; as of October 2026 it is not yet in force. Wording is our summary; only the official text is legally binding. (2026-10)

TopicRuleWhat applies
EU-resident sport shooter at a competitionCode de la sécurité intérieure, Art. R316-11 ↗A sport shooter resident in another EU country may bring up to six firearms listed in the European Firearms Pass without prior authorisation. They must carry a written invitation or proof of registration for an official competition stating date and venue, and show it on request.
EU-resident hunterCode de la sécurité intérieure, Art. R316-11 ↗A hunter resident in another EU country may bring up to three category C hunting guns and up to 100 cartridges per gun without prior authorisation, if they are listed in the European Firearms Pass and the hunter has a hunting licence and proof of the trip's purpose.
EU resident travelling for another purposeCode de la sécurité intérieure, Art. R316-10 ↗For any other purpose than a competition or hunting, category A, B and C firearms need the prior authorisation of a French prefect, entered in the European Firearms Pass for one or several trips over up to one year.
Non-EU visitor at a competitionArrêté du 8 juillet 2015 (modifié), régime d'admission temporaire ↗Bringing firearms from outside the EU normally needs a customs import authorisation (AIMG), but a participant in an international competition is exempt if they hold proof of registration with date and venue. Guns and ammunition (no quantity limit) must be declared under temporary admission at the first customs office on entering the EU; no export licence is needed on leaving.
Non-EU hunterArrêté du 8 juillet 2015 (modifié), régime d'admission temporaire ↗A non-EU hunter may bring two category C hunting guns and up to 100 cartridges per gun without an AIMG, if they can prove the purpose (e.g. a hunting invitation) and declare the guns at the first EU customs office.

Italy: bringing a shotgun to a competition

As across the EU, Regulation 2021/57 (REACH, since 15 Feb 2023) applies: no firing lead shot in wetlands or within 100 m of them. The national rule for Natura 2000 sites goes further on distance (150 m from the shore); regions implement it through their own acts, so details may vary. We found no separate national lead rule for clay ranges. In June 2026 the REACH Committee approved a wider restriction on lead in hunting and sport-shooting ammunition with a transition period; as of October 2026 it is not yet in force. Wording is our summary; only the official text is legally binding. (2026-10)

TopicRuleWhat applies
EU-resident sport shooter or hunterDecreto legislativo 30 dicembre 1992, n. 527, Art. 9, commi 1 e 3 ↗A sport shooter or hunter resident in another EU country may bring the guns listed in the European Firearms Pass without any other licence or permit; Italian numerical limits still apply. The purpose of the trip (e.g. a competition invitation) must be proved on police request.
EU resident travelling for another purposeDecreto legislativo 30 dicembre 1992, n. 527, Art. 5 ↗If the trip is not for a competition or hunting, prior consent of the Italian authority (issued by the Chief of Police) is needed and must be recorded in the European Firearms Pass. (not confirmed by an official text)
Temporary import for a competitionDecreto Ministeriale 5 giugno 1978 (GU n. 18 del 18 gennaio 1979), Art. 4 ↗A competitor from abroad brings guns on a special declaration from the national federation (FITAV for clay shooting), endorsed by the border police. It lists the competitions, the guns (no more than three) and the ammunition (no more than 1,000 cartridges). EU residents with a European Firearms Pass do not need the border police endorsement.
Non-EU visitor: declaration and time limitDecreto Ministeriale 5 giugno 1978, Artt. 5, 8, 9 ↗At the border you must declare in writing to the police where you will stay with the guns, and repeat the declaration if you move elsewhere. Temporary import lasts at most 90 days with no extension; the declaration is handed back to the border police on leaving.
Non-EU hunterDecreto Ministeriale 5 giugno 1978, Artt. 2–3 ↗To bring up to two hunting guns and up to 200 cartridges, a certificate from the Italian consulate in the country of departure, endorsed by the border police, is enough. Guns may be carried only in the open season and with third-party liability insurance.

Spain: bringing a shotgun to a competition

As across the EU, Regulation 2021/57 (REACH, since 15 Feb 2023) applies: no firing lead shot in wetlands or within 100 m of them. Spain's national rules matter for clay shooting too: they expressly cover sport shooting, so a range in such a zone cannot use lead shot. Hunting is a matter for the autonomous communities; two whose official texts we checked are listed below, others may have their own rules. In June 2026 the REACH Committee approved a wider restriction on lead in hunting and sport-shooting ammunition with a transition period; as of October 2026 it is not yet in force. Wording is our summary; only the official text is legally binding. (2026-10)

TopicRuleWhat applies
EU-resident sport shooter or hunterReal Decreto 137/1993, Reglamento de Armas (mod. Real Decreto 726/2020), Art. 112.4 ↗A sport shooter resident in another EU country may bring competition guns listed in the European Firearms Pass without prior authorisation, if they can prove the purpose, notably with a competition invitation. Hunters may do the same with hunting guns; no fee may be charged for accepting the pass.
EU resident travelling for another purposeReal Decreto 137/1993, Reglamento de Armas, Art. 112.1, 112.3 ↗In other cases an authorisation from the Guardia Civil is needed, entered in the European Firearms Pass for one or several trips over up to one year.
Non-EU visitor at a competitionReal Decreto 137/1993, Reglamento de Armas, Art. 111 ↗A non-EU competitor may get a special permit for their own guns, no more than six, usable only at authorised ranges and competition venues. The Spanish federation or the organiser applies to the Guardia Civil at least 15 days ahead; the shooter fills in a declaration shown to the arms control office at the point of entry, and outside training and competition the guns are kept by the organiser.
Non-EU hunterReal Decreto 137/1993, Reglamento de Armas, Art. 110 ↗A non-EU hunter may get a special permit for up to three hunting guns for three months, via a Spanish embassy or consulate or at the point of entry; a passport, home-country gun permits translated into Spanish and a list of hunting locations are required.

Czechia: bringing a shotgun to a competition

As across the EU, Regulation 2021/57 (REACH, since 15 Feb 2023) applies: no firing lead shot in wetlands or within 100 m of them. We found no separate national lead rule for clay ranges; ranges follow the terms of their own permits. Since 1 January 2026 the new Firearms Act No. 90/2024 Coll. applies, replacing Act No. 119/2002 Coll. Wording is our summary; only the official text is legally binding. (2026-10)

TopicRuleWhat applies
EU-resident sport shooter or hunterZákon č. 90/2024 Sb., o zbraních a střelivu, § 103 odst. 1 a 2 ↗A holder of a European Firearms Pass issued by another EU country may bring and use the guns listed in it for sport shooting or hunting without any other prior permit. They must be able to prove the purpose, e.g. with a competition invitation.
AmmunitionZákon č. 90/2024 Sb., o zbraních a střelivu, § 97 odst. 2 ↗Ammunition may be carried with the guns in a quantity matching the purpose of the temporary stay; the act sets no fixed number.
Non-EU visitorZákon č. 90/2024 Sb., o zbraních a střelivu, § 97 odst. 1, § 98 ↗A visitor without a European Firearms Pass needs a firearms escort permit (zbrojní průvodní list), issued by a Czech embassy, the Police Presidium or the police at a border crossing. The application states the guns, the number of cartridges, proof of the right to hold them, and the purpose and dates of the trip; it is valid for the trip, at most one year.
Notice at the borderZákon č. 90/2024 Sb., o zbraních a střelivu, § 11 odst. 1 písm. h) ↗Anyone crossing at a border checkpoint must tell the police they are travelling with guns or ammunition. In practice this concerns the Schengen external border, such as an airport with non-Schengen flights.

key_points.html: Outside the EU each country has its own rules: check them for each trip.
A temporary import permit is usually needed, and it takes weeks.
Show the gun to customs, fill in the declaration and keep it.
The organiser and your federation can help with documents.
No permit in time? Hire a gun at the destination.

quiz.q: What is usually needed to bring a gun into a country outside the EU?

options.text: Only the plane ticket and a gun case
A temporary import permit from that country
Nothing, if you have shot there before

quiz.explain: Each country has its own rules, and a temporary permit is most often required.

quiz.q: Why keep the customs declaration for the gun?

options.text: To sell the gun at the destination
To pay a lower fee on your next trip
To bring the gun back home without trouble

quiz.explain: The declaration shows that it is the same gun you brought in and are taking out.

quiz.q: What can you do if the permit will not be ready in time?

options.text: Hire a gun at the destination
Pack the gun in your suitcase anyway
Send the gun to the ground by post

quiz.explain: Taking a gun without the permits is not allowed; hiring one at the ground is the lawful option.
